The test image shows dried soybean stems with:
- Bleached/white stem tissue (straw-colored)
- Distinctive circular/oval dark pycnidia (fruiting bodies) embedded throughout the stem surface
- Dark necrotic coloration at the stem top
- Split/shredded stem texture

The Diaporthe reference confirms: the bottom-right panel shows a bleached stem with dark pycnidia markings that closely match the test image's characteristic oval dark structures on whitened stem tissue. This is the hallmark of Diaporthe stem canker — bleached white stems with embedded pycnidia visible as dark oval/ring shapes.
